defects: Drops the hypothesis `[Module.Invertible R M]` (M is an invertible R-module) entirely; this is the essential content of the informal statement ('invertible module ... rank one')

Replaces it with an unrelated, much stronger extraneous hypothesis `hM : ∀ s : R, Module.Free R (Localization.Away s ⊗[R] M)`, which already asserts freeness of the localization at *every* single ring element (not just a finite generating set), trivializing the theorem (e.g. S = {1} with hM 1 suffices) and having nothing to do with invertibility

As a result the produced theorem is not a formalization of the informal claim: instead of deriving Zariski-local freeness from invertibility, it assumes (an even stronger form of) the conclusion as a hypothesis
Conclusion uses `Localization.Away s ⊗[R] M` in place of gold's `LocalizedModule.Away r M`; while isomorphic as constructions, this is a different (non-primitive) formulation of the localized module
